ingress: UX designer at Tribia, working on Interaxo, with a master's degree in Media and Interaction Design from the University of Bergen. I enjoy making the complex understandable – working across the whole design process, from interviews and workshops to prototypes and usability testing.

lenker.tittel: Master's thesis – Data visualization for students with low to medium visual literacy
lenker.tekst: Media and Interaction Design, University of Bergen, 2024 (in Norwegian)

prosjekter.kort: A desktop interface that lets students interact with co-created data visualizations, using real emission data to enhance the credibility and context of a true use case.
oppsummering: A desktop interface that makes real emission data understandable for students
Three views: Compare, Explore and Verify
Built on six interviews, an expert focus group and a co-creation workshop with eight students
Three prototype iterations, each followed by usability testing
prosjekter.utfordring: Design a desktop interface that visualizes complex data for students. Imagine an interface transforming complex data into captivating stories that practically anyone can understand. This is the vision of FUSE – an innovative data visualization interface developed for and by students. Through an iterative design process, FUSE has developed into a prototype that uses authentic data and real text examples, to replace placeholders and imprecise visualizations that lead to confusion.

losning.tekst: Lets the user compare the size difference of separate categories. A vertical bar chart, represented as animated smoke coming out of an industrial pipe – the higher the bar, the darker and denser it becomes, just like smoke in real life.
Lets the user explore the development of each category. A line chart where the data points indicate whether there has been an increase, decrease or no change from the previous year.
Lets the user verify the values and sources behind the visualizations. A table with the exact values from the data set, where arrows show an increase (red) or decrease (green) from the year before.

prosess.tekst: Six interviews with students from different backgrounds and study programs identified their knowledge of and interest in climate, media habits, preferred ways to interact and thoughts on data visualization. This formed the basis of our target group.

A focus group with experts validated the interview findings and compared the students' needs to business interests and technical constraints, making it easier to prioritize and understand the decision-making behind a data visualization.

sitater: What is important depends on the purpose
The purpose of data visualization, in my opinion, is to convey a message
The storytelling should emphasize something and fit the environment

prosess.tekst: A co-creation workshop with eight students in four parts: individual work (Crazy 8 and storyboards), presentation and feedback using the optimist, pessimist and opportunist roles, group work, and a final vote.

deler.tekst: Each participant sketched ideas on their own, using Crazy 8 and storyboards.
Everyone presented their ideas, and the others gave feedback wearing one of three hats.

roller.tekst: Share what you believe is good and should be further focused on.
Share problem areas and challenges that may lead to conflict.
Share how things could be done differently or better.

deler.tekst: In groups, the participants combined the strongest ideas into shared concepts.
The groups presented their concepts, and each participant placed dot stickers on the ideas they believed in most.

bilder.tittel: Concept: a flight across the map
bilder.tekst: A world map with a plane over each region. Tapping a plane opens the emission data for that country, so the user explores the numbers by travelling across the map. The orange dots are the participants' votes.

A news-article concept, "Emissions in Norway or elsewhere". Each bar in the chart is smoke rising from a factory chimney, so higher emissions look like more smoke. A fact box explains definitions, where the emissions come from, emissions per person and CO₂ equivalents, with sources. The smoke metaphor became the starting point for the Compare view in FUSE.

prosess.tekst: The first iteration was a paper prototype inspired by the mockups, slightly adjusted to fit the personas and available data that we could find. We sketched every component we wanted to implement on an A3 paper, to make it appear as a desktop interface.

merker.tekst: Allows the user to toggle between three different views: a bar chart/pictogram, line chart or table.
Allows the user to narrow down the data displayed, either by transport or counties.
Provides the user with context of the data visualization.

prosess.tekst: The paper prototype was tested in quick 15-minute sessions with students recruited around campus.

funn.tekst: The filter menu was too big

prosess.tekst: A mid-fidelity prototype in Figma with a predefined user journey, built on real emission data and real text examples instead of placeholders.

merker.tekst: Toggles between emissions, development over time and the table.
Transport type and county, now with every county in Norway.
Explains the numbers in plain language, with an everyday comparison.

prosess.tekst: A side-by-side test compared horizontal and vertical bar charts and the right amount of data to visualize.

funn.tekst: Wanted to compare data with other countries

prosess.tekst: The third iteration became the final prototype – the solution shown at the top. Compared to the second prototype:
punkter: After the side-by-side test, the bars became vertical – the smoke now rises from industrial pipes, so higher emissions look like taller, darker smoke.
The views got clear, action-based names – Compare, Explore and Verify – instead of “See emissions”, “See development” and “See table”.
Change over time is visible at a glance: data points in the line chart and arrows in the table show whether emissions went up, down or stayed the same.

prosess.tekst: The final prototype was tested with three students. No changes were made after this last round.

funn.tekst: Most liked how the data was presented
Still wanted to compare with data from other countries

prosjekter.kort: An augmented reality application that lets users immerse themselves as a wizard, using full-body movement as input instead of the limited interactions common in AR mobile games.
oppsummering: An AR app in Unity where full-body movement is the input
The user becomes a wizard, casting magic with hand movements
A team of four with no prior Unity experience
Four approaches to hand tracking explored – position recognition proved most reliable
prosjekter.utfordring: Develop a prototype in Unity focusing on Augmented Reality and Body Interaction. None of the four of us had prior experience with Unity, and the task was very open-ended – so everyone created a storyboard, and we voted on the proposal we liked best.

losning.tekst: The user becomes a wizard, and the phone camera turns the room into the game. A glow shows that the right hand is tracked, hand movements conjure magical items like a dragon egg, and new movements move them, change them or trigger special effects. The hand is tracked with position recognition: actions fire when the hand enters predefined areas of the screen.

prosess.tekst: With an open-ended brief and no prior Unity experience, everyone in the team sketched a storyboard of their own idea. We voted on the proposal we liked best: a wizard who casts spells with hand movements.

All interactions are made with the user's right hand: a glow indicating that the hand is tracked, creating a virtual object by hand movement, moving and modifying it, and movements that trigger special effects.
Our preferred solution, with the potential to recognize multiple postures and movements – but with our experience and time limits, we never managed to recognize a specific hand posture.
If the script could recognize shapes drawn by the hand, different magic tricks could be triggered for different shapes.
Interacting with hidden game objects to change the colour of the hand glow – easier said than done when the objects are invisible.
The approach we chose: predefined areas that trigger actions when the hand enters them.

prosjekter.rolle: UX design, in collaboration with Wolftech
prosjekter.kort: Three designs that make journalists' research process more efficient and interactive in Wolftech's news production platform.
oppsummering: Making journalists' research faster in Wolftech's news production platform
Run as a Google Design Sprint together with Wolftech employees
Three concepts: Dashboard, Discover and Keyword search
Five expert interviews, three prototype iterations and two rounds of user testing over Zoom
prosjekter.utfordring: How can we improve an existing solution in an established news production platform? Wolftech described Feeds as a tool in its early stage that had not been given much attention yet. Our challenge was to look at how journalists do research, and how Feeds can make the research process easier and more efficient.

losning.tekst: A modular dashboard the journalist puts together from widgets – local news, press contacts, traffic updates, weather warnings and wire feeds. Content, size and position are entirely up to the user.
News stories filtered by the user's preferences and placed on a map, so the journalist can open a story and explore what else is happening in the same area.
An integrated search that narrows down the content in the Feeds columns, with sorting by top stories, newest, oldest or alphabetically, and columns the user can edit.

prosess.tekst: Five interviews over Zoom with experienced journalists from different newsrooms, to understand how they research a story, what slows them down and what motivates them.
A Google Design Sprint together with Wolftech employees, run as three workshops.

deler.tekst: We mapped the journalist's research process in a high-level map and turned the pain points into How Might We questions. A dot vote picked the questions worth solving.

lapper.tekst: HMW make it easier to know where the best resources are
HMW make it easier for journalists to get in contact with sources
HMW make it easier to find content that is interesting for the story

deler.tekst: Everyone sketched on their own in four steps, going from rough notes to a detailed solution sketch.
The strongest solution sketches were combined into a storyboard – the blueprint for the first prototype.

prosess.tekst: The first prototype built on the storyboard, to complement the existing Feed function in Wolftech News. We listed five ideas to prototype – Dashboard, Statistics, Collaboration, Keywords and Personalisation – and each group member drafted one. A vote decided which idea to take further: Keywords, which became a keyword search with an advanced filter.

The goal was to find out whether the keyword search and advanced filter worked for our target group. Since most Wolftech customers are international news agencies, we tested over Zoom and followed the participants through screen sharing. The hectic everyday life of journalists made them close to impossible to recruit, so we had to settle for participants outside the target group.

deler.tekst: We sorted and prioritized the feedback from the tests in an affinity map, grouped by feature.

prosess.tekst: We reviewed the test results, decided which direction to go, and took a step back to bring in the drafts from earlier.

deler.tekst: The Wolftech staff prioritized types of journalists by spending money from an imaginary, limited budget. The breaking news journalist came out on top.
Together with the Wolftech employees, we made a solution sketch focused on personalization and the individual needs of each journalist.

prosess.tekst: The main focus was a dashboard with everything a journalist needs at a glance. Instead of improving existing solutions, we tried new ones – which opened up a lot of possibilities. The user can move between a Dashboard with widgets, a Discover page, a pre-designed, curated Feeds page and a personal Feed page.

The goal was to see how the target group perceived the new concepts – Dashboard, Discover and Keyword search. We expected most participants to be active users of the Wolftech system, but only one of our three journalists was. The feedback was valuable, but too thin to draw firm conclusions from.

The feedback on the design and its direction was positive, but getting the right participants was still our main struggle. We designed our own iteration workshop to decide which part of the prototype needed more focus, and how to reach the target group.

deler.tekst: The sailboat exercise split the feedback into what pushed the design forward and what held it back, grouped by topic – a visual way to see where the main issues were.
Every participant had one vote, choosing between Dashboard, Discover, BBC Desk and My Feed. Discover won and became the main focus moving forward.

prosjekter.rolle: UX design, in collaboration with TV 2
prosjekter.kort: An exploration mode for TV 2 Play, tailored to young adults with children – designed so that exciting content finds the user, not the other way around.
oppsummering: An exploration mode for TV 2 Play, aimed at young adults with children
Lets relevant content find the user – less scrolling, fewer cancellations
A visual identity inspired by the universe
Interviews, think-aloud sessions and two rounds of usability testing
prosjekter.utfordring: Design a user interface in collaboration with TV 2 for their streaming service TV 2 Play, tailored to young adults with children. The challenge in streaming services is finding the balance between too much and too little content on the home page – showing users that there is plenty of exciting content for them, without overwhelming them.

losning.tekst: A visual design inspired by the universe – a universe of undiscovered content, sparking curiosity with color contrasts, varying shapes and figures.
Breaking away from the monotonous presentation of the streaming giants with creative shapes, sizes and colors. XPLORE is unique for each user, reflecting their personal interests.
A positive filter bubble that minimizes scrolling, frustration and uninteresting recommendations, which can lead to subscription cancellations.

prosess.tekst: Interviews with young adults with children about their use of and preferences for streaming services.
Three participants navigated TV 2 Sumo, NRK TV or Netflix while sharing their thoughts.
A simple prototype to test our ideas: dragging favorite categories up and down, further filtering for more personalized content, and the best possible alternative when a title isn't available.
Two iterations with three participants each, analyzing the results and updating the prototype after each round.

prosjekter.rolle: Individual project, exchange at Bath Spa University
prosjekter.kort: A 3D model and short movie of Bath City FC's football stadium, made in Autodesk Maya with no prior 3D experience.
oppsummering: A 3D model and short film of Bath City FC's stadium
Made in Autodesk Maya with no prior 3D experience
Based on online research and my own photos from the stadium
Exchange project at Bath Spa University
prosjekter.utfordring: Create a piece of environment modelling that responded to my experience of Bath with the 3D software Autodesk Maya, and make a short movie. I chose Twerton Park, the football stadium of Bath City FC, because I spent a lot of my time in England travelling around to watch football matches.

prosess.tekst: Gathered pictures of Twerton Park from the web and visited the stadium myself to take pictures.
With no prior 3D experience, I learned Maya's most important features through a tutorial from our tutor and built the model using polygonal modelling.

prosjekter.rolle: Individual project, exchange at Bath Spa University
prosjekter.kort: A landscape of my own choice and a short film of a car driving through it, made in Cinema 4D and Adobe After Effects.
oppsummering: A landscape and short film of a car driving through it
Modelled in Cinema 4D and edited in Adobe After Effects
Car, road, bridge and landscape – plus a boat, a house and flowers
Exchange project at Bath Spa University
prosjekter.utfordring: Create a landscape of our own choice and make a short film with a car driving through the landscape. We used Cinema 4D during the last three weeks of the course, after being introduced to Adobe Animate and Adobe After Effects.

prosess.tekst: Started with the car and the road, and worked on getting the car to drive smoothly – the most difficult part was getting it over the bridge.
Added mountains, grass, water, trees and stones – and since it took less time than expected, also a boat, a house and flowers.
Placed cameras in the scene, made different clips and rendered the short film in Adobe After Effects.
